input.rule: Parse 256 printed two-character base-60 cells as bytes using 0–9,A–Z,a–x; 32×8 grid row and column readings.

scope: Exact Stage X4 component, not its X1/X2/X3 statistical or integer tests. Four complete grid readings: R, R reversed, C, C reversed. Five source decoders: zlib raw DEFLATE, zlib, gzip, bzip2, LZMA auto; plus previously documented Stage N offset-zero signatures.
source_null: For each decoder, 100,000 seeded iid-uniform 256-byte blocks using NumPy default_rng(seed=3321). Source records fraction reaching decoder EOF. It declares PASS only when EOF and estimated rate ×20≤0.01; EOF with higher rate is inconclusive; no EOF is EXCLUDED.
source_decoder_semantics: One decoder call, output cap 1 MiB; eof must be reached, but source does not require input fully consumed and does not test meaningfulness of output. An output hitting the cap without EOF is not a proof of invalid format. No offsets/prefixes or additional transforms.
post_replay_controls: After source replay, test synthetic complete streams for each of five codecs, plus truncated and trailing-junk cases. These are implementation diagnostics, not preregistered source power controls and do not retroactively validate a broad negative conclusion.
limitations: Only printed-grid bytes in four routes under those five complete-stream decoder APIs. Raw DEFLATE can produce EOF on random input (~0.0055 in source null), making an isolated EOF inconclusive. Zero calibrator hits for other codecs gives a finite-sample upper limit, not a true zero probability. Other byte parsing, uncertain cells, file offsets, keyed/composed transforms and >1MiB outputs remain untested.
